extracted.intended_audience: comedy writers and performers learning misdirection techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and evaluating jokes that use misdirection — leading the audience toward one interpretation in the setup and delivering a twist or punchline that reveals a different, retroactively-valid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-up / payoff structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the classic set-up/payoff device: the setup creates expectations and the payoff subverts them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a setup that clearly establishes an expectation and a payoff that reverses or reframes that expectation. Ensure the setup contains the material necessary to make the payoff intelligible in retrospect; avoid throwaway setups that don't connect to the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious first interpretation primed by the setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an obvious first interpretation primed by the setup?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The setup should actively encourage the audience to adopt one interpretation. Techniques: selective wording, emphasis in delivery, or narrative sequencing that biases understanding. Anti-pattern: a weak or ambiguous setup that fails to steer the audience toward any particular reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second (punchline) interpretation is valid in retrospect
rubrics_metrics.description: The second (punchline) interpretation must also be valid when looking back at the setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punchline should not rely on impossibility or contradiction — after the reveal, the audience should see how the setup could plausibly have supported the alternate reading. Scoring guidance: higher marks when the alternate reading feels inevitable in hindsight rather than contrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second interpretation hidden enough to be surprising
rubrics_metrics.description: The second interpretation must be hidden sufficiently during the setup so it produces surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance is key: the alternate reading must be available but unlikely to be noticed during the setup. If it's too obvious, there is no surprise; if it's impossible to infer from the setup, the reveal feels arbitrary. Anti-patterns: telegraphing the twist too early or making the twist logically disconnected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup actively guides toward the wrong interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the setup actively guide toward the wrong interpretation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use linguistic cues, salient details, and sequencing to bias audience inference toward the intended (but ultimately incorrect) reading. Delivery choices (timing, emphasis) can strengthen the misdirection. Anti-pattern: neutral presentation that fails to mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal is clean — not just confusing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the reveal clear and comprehensible rather than merely confusing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punchline should resolve tension by making the alternate interpretation clear; confusion indicates a failure to link setup and payoff. Prefer reveals that immediately click for the audience and produce recognition rather than bewilderment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both interpretations must be available in principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the initial and the punchline interpretations must be supported by the material — each must be a legitimate reading of the setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft wording or structure that permits two readings; ambiguity can be syntactic, semantic, or contextual. Example: garden-path constructions where the parser initially selects one parse but a later element forces reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden-path sentence (syntactic misdirection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use syntactic ambiguity to mislead the parser (e.g., 'The horse raced past the barn fell.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create sentences that the listener's usual syntactic parsing will misread, and then force a reparse at the end. Guidance: keep the sentence grammatical in both readings and ensure the reparse produces the punchline effect. Anti-pattern: using ungrammatical or unresolvable constructions that leave the audience lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pull-back-and-reveal (long buildup with twist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a long buildup that is recast by a later twist which reframes earlier material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a narrative or extended premise that seems to aim at one conclusion, then 'pull back' to reveal a different, comedic interpretation. Ensure the reveal rereads earlier beats coherently; pacing and timing are crucial to maintain tension until the payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play with audience assumptions to create contrast and surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit audience assumptions to create a delightful contrast between expectation and outcome, adding surprise, wit, and unpredictability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify commonplace assumptions the audience will make and design the setup to trigger them. Use the payoff to subvert those assumptions in a way that feels witty rather than mean-spirited. Anti-patterns: subversions that rely on offensive stereotypes or that produce discomfort rather than humor.
